How this was found

a climb is circling flight of at least 60 s with at least 80 m height gain, counted only after the engine stopped (detected with the logger's noise sensor). Flights from Kiripotib and Bitterwasser are included. Ground source: the wind is measured from how each glider's circles drift (median of all climbs within 45 min and 60 km), and each thermal is traced back down to the terrain using the climb rate plus 0.8 m/s glider sink. Climbs entered more than 2,500 m above ground are left out of the ground view. Typical shift is 1–3 km upwind; accuracy about 1 km. Climbs within 2.5 km of each other were grouped together, and a group counts as a hotspot when at least 7 flights, 3 pilots and 3 different days used it, so one pilot's habits or one busy day don't create a hotspot. The heatmap divides, for each 1 km square, the number of flights that climbed near it by the number that flew near it, smoothed and compared with the average for the whole area (about 7%). D-KJPL (two pilots) counts as one pilot. Time windows are by local clock time. Heights are GPS altitude MSL; Veronica is about 1,345 m. Times are local (UTC+2). With this many flights it's a pattern, not proof. Thermals drift downwind and depend on the day. Roads, towns and airfields come from the XCSoar Namibia map; airspace from your OpenSoar airspace file. Not for navigation.
